title: Relationships, Ownership, and Record Lifecycle
readerIntent: Design relationships without losing module ownership or tenant safety.
owner: Each module owns its schemas; references preserve the target module authority
summary: Relationships may connect schemas in the same or different modules, but creation, validation, access, and lifecycle remain governed by each owning capability.

sections.heading: Relationship choices
items: Embed a value only when it has no independent identity or lifecycle.
Reference an existing record when another capability owns it or it is reused.
Create a related record through the related schema contract when the user has permission and no suitable record exists.
Use explicit parent, child, collection, and ownership metadata rather than inferring relationships from labels.

sections.heading: Cross-module relationships
paragraphs: An Enterprise can reference a Tenant even though profile-owned contracts govern both models, and other capabilities can reference those records without taking ownership. When related schemas belong to different modules, the caller must use the target module contract or a governed coordinating service; it must not write the target collection directly.

sections.heading: Lifecycle questions
items: Can a related record exist independently?
Which capability authorizes create, update, unlink, archive, or delete?
What happens when a parent is deactivated or removed?
Are tenant, enterprise, catalog, version, and ownership boundaries compatible?
Must changes publish, index, invalidate cache, emit an event, or begin a workflow?

sections.heading: Relationship types and meaning
items: Required and optional single references express whether one target is necessary.
Collection references require duplicate, ordering, minimum, and maximum behavior.
Composition means the child lifecycle is normally controlled by the parent.
Association means each side retains an independent lifecycle.
Hierarchy needs distinct parent and child labels plus cycle protection.
paragraphs: The schema records business meaning, not merely a database identifier. Cardinality, ownership, selection, nested creation, unlinking, and deletion are explicit contract decisions.

sections.heading: Friendly identity and discovery
paragraphs: Related-record selectors show safe identity such as code and description, not only an opaque key. Axis displays code plus a short description and makes the complete description available as a tooltip.
Search remains authorized and tenant-scoped. Friendly display fields improve usability but cannot expose inaccessible records.

sections.heading: Select existing or create related
paragraphs: A schema-driven form can offer Select existing and Create new. Create new appears only when the target model exposes creation and the employee has permission. The rule applies to same-module and cross-module relationships.
Nested creation calls the target capability's normal API and validation. After success, the identifier joins the parent draft. Failure must not leave a partially saved parent.

sections.heading: Example: Enterprise relationships
paragraphs: An Enterprise belongs to a Tenant, may have a Parent enterprise, and may relate to addresses and contacts. Role-specific labels prevent two unrelated fields from both appearing simply as Enterprise.
When the required Tenant is absent, an authorized employee can create it through Profile's Tenant contract. Tenant permissions, uniqueness, and validation remain Profile-owned.

sections.heading: Cross-module authority
items: The source model validates whether the association is allowed.
The target capability validates existence and visibility.
Creation, update, and deletion use the target public contract.
A stored foreign identifier does not grant authorization.
Cache, search, import, export, and event projections preserve both scopes.

sections.heading: Deletion and lifecycle behavior
items: Restrict deletion while required dependents exist.
Detach optional associations only through an authorized mutation.
Cascade only for genuine composition and document recovery.
Use deactivation or archival when audit, publishing, or retention prevents deletion.
Reconcile search, cache, exports, events, and online projections.

sections.heading: Verification matrix
items: Valid existing selection and permitted nested creation.
Missing, duplicate, wrong-type, and nonexistent references.
Unauthorized visibility and wrong-tenant association.
Parent cycles and collection cardinality boundaries.
Child failure, parent failure, retry, and partial-state recovery.
Delete, detach, deactivate, archive, import, export, and search behavior.
